additions.title: RSTS/E V9.0 login and logout
additions.text: The RSTS/E V9.0 System User’s Guide describes HELLO or LOGIN followed by the User prompt for a PPN and then Password. Password characters are not displayed. LOGOUT and BYE end the terminal session; LOGOUT defaults to /FULL, with /BRIEF also available. Ending a login session is not a system shutdown procedure. These are V9.0 DCL instructions, not verified commands for every RSTS/E release or run-time system.
additions.keywords: hello login logout bye ppn session rsts90-session
additions.question: Explain RSTS/E V9.0 login and logout.

additions.title: RSTS/E V9.0 directory and file display
additions.text: In the RSTS/E V9.0 DCL environment, DIRECTORY displays file information; TYPE displays an individual file’s contents. With no file specification, DIRECTORY lists the user directory on the public structure. The guide distinguishes file information from file contents. This note covers V9.0 and supplies no device installation or system shutdown sequence.
additions.keywords: directory files listing type public structure rsts90-directory
additions.question: Explain RSTS/E V9.0 directory and file display.

additions.title: RSX-11M-PLUS V3.0, July 1985: PIP directory listing
additions.text: This edition of the shared RSX-11M/M-PLUS Utilities Manual explicitly covers RSX-11M V4.2 and RSX-11M-PLUS V3.0. PIP’s /LI switch lists selected files in a UFD with status information. /BR, /FU and /TB select alternate listing formats. Without an output listing-file specification, output defaults to TI:. This is a PIP utility description, not a universal DCL command or evidence of an installed driver.
additions.question: Explain RSX-11M-PLUS V3.0, July 1985: PIP directory listing.

additions.title: Deferred pointers and the stack pointer
additions.text: @(Rn)+ is autoincrement deferred, mode 3: the register points to a word containing the operand address and advances by two, including byte instructions. @-(Rn) is mode 5: subtract two before fetching the word pointer. R6/SP autoincrement and autodecrement always step by two, including byte operations. In contrast, INCB -(R0) decrements R0 by one before access. The PDP-11/70 has three mode-selected R6 registers, with one active at a time.
additions.keywords: deferred pointer stack autoincrement autodecrement r6 1170-deferred-stack
